title: Why Humanity Will Never Leave The Solar System

sentences.en: The latest limited edition pin is here.
sentences.jp: 最新の限定ピンがここにあります。

sentences.en: Now available on the Kurz Gesagt shop.
sentences.jp: Kurz Gesagtのショップで現在販売中です。

sentences.en: You will never leave the solar system.
sentences.jp: あなたは太陽系を永遠に離れることはありません。

sentences.en: Nobody alive today will, and maybe no human ever.
sentences.jp: 今日生きている誰もがそうなりません。また、おそらく人類の誰もがそうなりません。

sentences.en: Locked in by an invisible barrier, impossible to overcome for carbon-based animals like us.
sentences.jp: 透明な壁によって閉じ込められており、私たちのような炭素基盤の動物にとって、この壁を突破することは不可能です。

vocab.note: This term is used as a past participle to describe a state of being restricted.
Adjective describing something that cannot be seen.
A physical or abstract obstacle that prevents progress.
To defeat or surmount a difficulty.
Refers to life forms primarily composed of carbon.

sentences.en: And not just us, there may be millions of alien civilizations in the universe, none of them ever able to venture into deep space in a meaningful way.
sentences.jp: 私たちだけではありません。宇宙に数百万の異星文明が存在する可能性がありますが、いずれも深宇宙への有意義な探索をすることはありません。

vocab.note: Societies with complex social structures and technological advancements.
To attempt something risky or difficult.
Having significance or purpose.

sentences.en: Okay, but how can this be?
sentences.jp: でも、どうしてこのことが可能なのか？

sentences.en: We've made countless videos imagining how the exploration of the galaxy and beyond should just be a question of time, sort of mandatory for civilizations at a certain point.
sentences.jp: 私たちが制作した無数の動画では、銀河系やそれ以上の探索が、特定の段階で必然的に時間の問題であると想定しています。

vocab.note: An extremely large number.
To form mental images or concepts.
宇宙の探査活動を指す。
星の集団で、太陽が含まれる銀河系を指す。
特定の条件のもとで避けられないこと。

sentences.en: But there's a catch.
sentences.jp: ただし、条件があります。

sentences.en: We're pushing up against fundamental physics.
sentences.jp: 我々は基本的な物理学にぶつかります。

vocab.meaning: 物理学の基本法則にぶつかる行為
vocab.note: This is a verb in the context of physics, indicating the action of encountering limits.
Adjective describing physics that is foundational.
The scientific study of matter and energy.

sentences.en: What is this barrier made of dust and nothingness?
sentences.jp: このバリアは、ほこりと空虚から成り立っていますか？

vocab.note: The state of being empty or void.

sentences.en: And why is it so hard to overcome?
sentences.jp: そして、なぜそれが克服するのが難しいのでしょうか？

sentences.en: You don't understand how large space is.
sentences.jp: あなたは空間の大きさを理解していません。

sentences.en: We don't either.
sentences.jp: 我々も同じです。

sentences.en: Conceptualizing the size of space is impossible for our ape brains that evolved to understand distances like right here and over the next hill.
sentences.jp: 私たちの猿の脳は、ここにとこの距離や、次に山の向こうの距離を理解するため進化したため、空間の規模を概念化することは不可能です。

vocab.note: To form abstract concepts or ideas.
Refers to human brains in this context.
To develop over time through natural selection.
The spatial separation between objects.

sentences.en: Space is so absurdly huge that we just check out and just hear very far.
sentences.jp: 空間は、私たちがただチェックアウトし、非常に遠くまで聞こえるほどに、信じられないほど巨大です。

vocab.meaning: 非常に不自然な、不思議な
vocab.note: This term describes something that is extremely illogical or unreasonable, often used to emphasize the vastness or scale of something.

sentences.en: Very far and > [ music ] > a million times very far feels the same.
sentences.jp: 非常に遠くで > [音楽] > 100万倍も遠くても同じように感じる。

sentences.en: But it's not.
sentences.jp: でも、違う。

sentences.en: To help our brains, let's start with what makes us cross distances, speed.
sentences.jp: 脳を助けるために、私たちが距離を越えるために必要な速度から始めましょう。

sentences.en: The fastest a human ever traveled in space were astronauts at 40, 000 km an hour returning from the moon in 1969.
sentences.jp: 人類が宇宙で最も速く移動したのは、1969年に月から帰還した宇宙飛行士が40,000km/hで行ったこと。

vocab.note: The term 'fastest' is an adjective meaning the highest speed or rate of movement among a group.
The term 'traveled' is a past tense verb meaning to move from one place to another, especially over a long distance.
The term 'astronauts' refers to individuals trained to travel in space, typically as part of a space mission.
The term 'returning' is a present participle of the verb 'return', meaning to come back to a place after leaving.

sentences.en: Not bad, but way too slow.
sentences.jp: まあ、遅いけど、あまりにも遅い。

sentences.en: The fastest thing humans have ever built by far is the Parker Solar Probe, which at this moment uses a physics cheat code hurling around the gravity well of Venus accelerating to get closer to the sun.
sentences.jp: 人類が作成した最も速い物は、今この瞬間、金星の重力井戸を通過して太陽に近づくための物理のクレートコードを活用しているパーカー太陽探査機です。

vocab.note: The term 'hurling' is a verb meaning to throw something forcefully, often used in the context of sports or physics.
The term 'gravity' refers to the force that attracts objects with mass toward one another, especially the Earth.

The term 'accelerating' refers to increasing speed or rate of motion, which is a key concept in physics. In this context, it describes the Parker Solar Probe's motion as it gains speed by using Venus's gravity.

sentences.en: After 7 years of doing this, the probe is shooting through space at a breathtaking 635, 000 km an hour, fast enough to go around the world in 4 minutes or to cover the distance from Earth to the moon in 36.
sentences.jp: 7年間この作業を続けた後、探査機は宇宙を4分で1回りする635,000km/hの速度で飛行しています。地球から月までの距離を36分で covers。

vocab.note: The term 'breathtaking' describes something extremely impressive or awe-inspiring. Here, it emphasizes the incredible speed of the Parker Solar Probe.

sentences.en: So, let's pretend we had a spaceship that fast with a human crew ready to explore the universe.
sentences.jp: だから、私たちが宇宙を探索するための、人間の乗組が整った高速船を仮に持っているとしましょう。

vocab.note: The verb 'pretend' means to imagine or assume something is true for the sake of argument. In this context, it's used to set up a hypothetical scenario about a fast spaceship.
A 'spaceship' is a vehicle designed for space travel. In this context, it's part of a hypothetical scenario where a spaceship is moving at an extremely high speed.
The verb 'explore' means to investigate or discover new areas. Here, it refers to the purpose of having a spaceship with a human crew: to explore the universe.

sentences.en: Current rockets would need 7 to 10 months to reach Mars, but our new spaceship covers the distance in just 2 weeks.
sentences.jp: 現在のロケットでは火星に到達するまでに7から10ヶ月かかりますが、私たちの新しい宇宙船はわずか2週間で距離を covers します。

vocab.meaning: 宇宙探査用のロケット
vocab.note: Current rockets would need 7 to 10 months to reach Mars, but our new spaceship covers the distance in just 2 weeks.
Current rockets would need 7 to 10 months to reach Mars, but our new spaceship covers the distance in just 2 weeks.

sentences.en: Pretty good.
sentences.jp: なかなか良いです。

sentences.en: The next stop is Pluto, which we'll reach after about a year.
sentences.jp: 次はプラネットが目的地で、約1年後には到達します。

sentences.en: Okay, much longer, but still okay.
sentences.jp: いいえ、かなり長いですが、それでも大丈夫です。

sentences.en: It only takes 2 more years to pass the heliopause and one more to pass Voyager 2, which traveled over 50 years to get this far.
sentences.jp: ヘリポーズを通過するまでに2年、そしてボイジャー2号を通過するまで1年かかります。ボイジャー2号は50年以上かけてここまで来たのです。

vocab.meaning: 太陽風が太陽系の外側に達する境界
vocab.note: It only takes 2 more years to pass the heliopause and one more to pass Voyager 2, which traveled over 50 years to get this far.

sentences.en: Great.
sentences.jp: Great.

sentences.en: The next stop is the end of the Oort Cloud, the true edge of the solar system, where open space begins.
sentences.jp: 次はオーツクラウドの端、太陽系の真の端で、開かれた空間が始まります。

sentences.en: We reach it in 2, 500 years.
sentences.jp: 2,500年後に到達します。

sentences.en: Oh.
sentences.jp: あっ

sentences.en: Oh, no.
sentences.jp: あっ、ない

sentences.en: Not only did we travel for the amount of time it took to get from the founding of the Roman Republic to the present day, there's nothing out here.
sentences.jp: ローマ共和国の成立から現在までにかかる時間にかけて旅をしたにもかかわらず、ここには何もない。

vocab.note: The founding of the Roman Republic refers to the establishment of the Roman Republic in 509 BCE.

sentences.en: This is the invisible barrier, the barrier of nothingness that might trap us in the solar system forever.
sentences.jp: この無視できる壁、太陽系に永続的に閉じ込められる可能性のある「何もない」壁だ。

sentences.en: Space tends to be like that.
sentences.jp: 宇宙はそういうものだ。

sentences.en: There is a place that's very far away, but with human ingenuity and billions of dollars, we can get there.
sentences.jp: とても遠い場所はあるが、人間の知恵と数十億ドルの資金があれば、そこに到達できる。

vocab.note: Ingenuity refers to the ability to come up with clever solutions to problems.
Billions refers to the large number 1,000,000,000 (one billion).

sentences.en: Then you zoom out one more time and all hope leaves your body.
sentences.jp: もう一度ズームアウトすると、すべての希望が体から消える。

sentences.en: And the problem is that we've barely started zooming out.
sentences.jp: 問題は、私たちがズームアウトをほとんど始めただけだということである。

vocab.note: Barely means almost but not quite, indicating a small amount.
Zooming refers to the action of magnifying or focusing on a small area.

sentences.en: Why don't we just go faster?
sentences.jp: なぜ、もっと速く進むことができないでしょうか？

sentences.en: Well, we don't know of a non-magic way to travel faster than light, teleport, or freeze people.
sentences.jp: ただ、光速を超える非魔法の方法、テレポート、または人を凍結する方法については、我々が知っているわけではありません。

vocab.meaning: 瞬間的に場所を移動する（魔法による）
vocab.note: 魔法を用いる場合の移動手段

vocab.meaning: 人を凍結する（魔法による）
vocab.note: 魔法を用いる場合の凍結手段

sentences.en: > [ music ] > So, no warp drive for now.
sentences.jp: > [音楽] > 今のところ、ワープドライブは使えません。

sentences.en: But, things like a propulsion system that uses nuclear fusion or antimatter, powerful enough to reach a substantial fraction of the speed of light, are in the realm of the physically possible.
sentences.jp: しかし、核融合や反物質を用いた推進システムが、光速の相当な分数に達するほど強力である場合、物理的に可能であると考えられます。

vocab.note: 核融合や反物質を用いる推進システム
核融合反応を用いた推進システム
反物質を用いた推進システム
速度のかなりの分数

sentences.en: Ignoring the technical details and various problems that these energy sources have, we'll be very optimistic and make the reasonable assumption that we can get a spaceship to fly at around 20% the speed of light, which is extremely fast, 60, 000 km per second, 216 million km per hour.
sentences.jp: 技術的な詳細やこれらのエネルギー源のさまざまな問題を無視し、非常にoptimisticに考えると、我々は合理的に仮定することができます。このスペースシャトルが光速の約20％、つまり60,000 km/s、216億km/hで飛行することができると。

vocab.meaning: 技術的詳細や問題を無視して

過度に楽観的な仮定
In this context, it refers to a reasonable guess made without detailed technical analysis.

sentences.en: Alpha Centauri, the closest star system to our own, in 20 years.
sentences.jp: 20年後には、私たちの近くにある最も近い星系、アラファ・センターリーに到達します。

vocab.note: Refers to the star system that is nearest to Earth in the context of the sentence.

sentences.en: We can work with that.
sentences.jp: それでいいよ。

sentences.en: There's only one small problem.
sentences.jp: ただ一つの小さな問題がある。

sentences.en: We don't have internet.
sentences.jp: インターネットがない。

sentences.en: Wait.
sentences.jp: 待って。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.jp: え？

sentences.en: Just kidding.

sentences.en: But our sponsor Saily can help you with that problem while traveling.
sentences.jp: しかし、私たちのスポンサーであるSailyは、旅中でもその問題を解決するのに役立つ。

vocab.note: A sponsor is someone or something that provides financial support for an event or project.

sentences.en: Saily is the eSIM service app from the creators of Nord VPN.
sentences.jp: SailyはNord VPNの作成者によるeSIMサービスアプリです。

vocab.note: Creators are the people who create or produce something, such as software or services.

sentences.en: You can choose from a wide range of affordable eSIM plans for over 200 destinations, so you'll never be without an internet connection while traveling.
sentences.jp: 旅行中でもインターネット接続が常に保たれるよう、200カ国以上で利用可能な安価なeSIMプランから選べます。

vocab.note: This term refers to something that is inexpensive or cost-effective.
Refers to places where travel is planned.

sentences.en: Just download the app, pick a data plan, use the code Kurzgesagt for a 15% discount on your first data package, and install the eSIM in advance.
sentences.jp: アプリをダウンロードし、データプランを選択後、最初のデータパッケージにKurzgesagtのコードで15%の割引を適用し、事前にeSIMをインストールしてください。

vocab.note: A reduction in price for a product or service.
A set of services or products offered together.
To set up software or hardware.

vocab.meaning: a German phrase meaning 'shortly' or 'briefly', used as a brand name for a YouTube channel
vocab.note: This is a brand name, not a standard English word

sentences.en: It'll activate automatically when you arrive, and you can start browsing right away.
sentences.jp: 到着すると自動的に有効になり、すぐにブラウジングを開始できます。

vocab.note: To make something functional or operational.
Without manual intervention.
To reach a place.
The act of using the internet to look for information.

sentences.en: You can also use Saily to feel like a local.
sentences.jp: Sailyを使用することで、地元の生活感を味わえます。

sentences.en: It now comes with an app-based phone number for voice calls and SMS that stays the same everywhere.
sentences.jp: 現在、世界中で同じアプリベースの電話番号が利用可能で、電話やSMSも変わりません。

sentences.en: > [ music ] > Perfect for local apps, shops, and travel companions, and to keep your real number private.
sentences.jp: > [ 音楽 ] > 地元のアプリ、店舗、旅行同伴者に最適で、実際の電話番号をプライベートに保ちます。

vocab.note: Context: Perfect for local apps, shops, and travel companions, and to keep your real number private.

sentences.jp: 1つのアプリダウンロードで、旅行中のインターネット問題を一括解決し、時間と高額なローミング料金を節約できます。

vocab.note: Context: With just one app download, you've solved your internet problem while traveling once and for all, saving time and expensive roaming fees.
Context: With just: one app download, you've solved your internet problem while traveling once and for all, saving time and expensive roaming fees.

sentences.jp: Sailyをダウンロードし、チェックアウト時にKurzgesagtのコードを使用するか、sailyにアクセスしてください。

vocab.note: Context: Download Saily and use the code Kurzgesagt at checkout, or go to saily.

sentences.en: com / kurzgesagt.
sentences.jp: com / kurzgesagt.

sentences.en: All you have to do is pick your next destination.
sentences.jp: 次に目的地を選ぶだけでいいんです。

vocab.meaning: the place you are going to or the end point of a journey
vocab.note: Commonly used in travel contexts

sentences.en: We'll go back to solving our trickier travel problems.
sentences.jp: もっと難しい旅の問題を解き明かしていきましょう。

vocab.meaning: the process of finding a solution to a problem
vocab.note: Present participle of 'solve'

vocab.meaning: more difficult or complex than something else
vocab.note: Comparative form of 'tricky'

sentences.en: Everything should be sorted out now, right?
sentences.jp: すべては今、整理されているはずなのに、 right?

vocab.meaning: arranged or organized in an orderly way
vocab.note: Informal term for 'resolved' or 'completed'

sentences.en: Well, there's only one small issue.
sentences.jp: でも、ちょっとだけ問題があります。

sentences.en: Space hates you.
sentences.jp: 空間はあなたを嫌います。

sentences.en: The barrier of dust.
sentences.jp: ほこりの壁

sentences.en: Unfortunately, we'll run into a few obstacles on the way.
sentences.jp: 残念ですが、途中でいくつかの障害にぶつかります。

vocab.meaning: difficulties or problems that one must overcome
vocab.note: Plural form of 'obstacle'

sentences.en: Literally.
sentences.jp: literally.

sentences.en: Because while space is very empty, > [ music ] > it's not actually empty.
sentences.jp: なぜなら、宇宙は非常に空虚であるが、> [音楽] > 実際には空ではないからだ。

sentences.en: There are energetic particles, gas, dust, and things bigger than dust.
sentences.jp: エネルギー粒子、ガス、塵、塵よりも大きい物質が存在するからだ。

vocab.note: This term describes particles with high energy, often used in physics contexts.
Fundamental units of matter in physics.

sentences.en: As a lot of unhappy people experience every day, if you're going really fast and smash into something, you have a huge problem.
sentences.jp: 毎日多くの不幸な人々が経験するように、非常に速く何かに衝突すると、大きな問題が生じる。

vocab.note: Feeling or being in a state of unhappiness.

sentences.en: And at 20% the speed of light, this is true even if the thing you're smashing into is just an atom.
sentences.jp: 20%の光速でこの現象は、原子すら衝突する場合でも真実である。

vocab.note: The action of colliding or smashing into something.

sentences.en: An individual iron atom that hits your spaceship at this speed has enough energy to carve a damage track tenths of a millimeter deep.
sentences.jp: この速度で衝突する1つの鉄原子は、あなたの宇宙船に十分なエネルギーをもっており、0.1ミリメートルほどの深さの傷を刻む。

vocab.note: Fractional unit representing one-tenth.
Unit of length equal to one-thousandth of a meter.

sentences.en: Over time, its hull would be riddled with microscopic bullet holes, which is not great.
sentences.jp: 時間の経過とともに、船の外皮には微細な銃孔が数多く生じ、これはあまり良くない。

vocab.note: To be filled with small holes or damage.
Very small, often invisible to the naked eye.
A projectile fired from a gun.

sentences.en: Of course, our engineers knew this and created a shield for our ship, a sort of protective cell that absorbs or at least slows down most molecules we smash into.
sentences.jp: もちろん、私たちのエンジニアはこのことを知っており、船に保護セルを作り上げ、私たちが衝突する分子のほとんどを吸収または少なくとも遅らせる。

vocab.note: Technical professionals who design and build systems
A protective barrier that defends against attacks
Relating to protection or defense
To take in or retain something
The smallest unit of a chemical compound

sentences.en: And while this makes the journey much safer, there are things floating around in space that are larger than atoms.
sentences.jp: この状況では旅がはるかに安全になる一方で、宇宙には原子よりも大きな物質が浮遊しています。

vocab.note: In the context of space, 'floating' refers to objects moving without gravity or support.

sentences.en: Running into a single grain of dust at 20% the speed of light is like running into a grenade, causing a tiny detonation as the dust explosively evaporates, grinding away our protective shield.
sentences.jp: 20%の光速で一粒のほこりにぶつかった場合、それはグランドに相当する爆発を引き起こし、ほこりが爆発的に蒸発して保護するシールドを粉々にします。

vocab.note: A grenade is a small explosive device that can be thrown or detonated remotely.
In this context, 'causing' describes the effect of running into dust at high speed.
The sudden and violent explosion of a substance, here referring to the dust.
Describes the rapid and violent nature of the dust's evaporation.
The process of a substance changing from liquid to gas, here describing dust.
In this context, 'grinding' refers to the abrasive action of the dust on the shield.

sentences.en: But you can also hit something bigger than a grain of dust, like a small rock the size of a golf ball.
sentences.jp: 一粒のほこりよりも大きな物質にぶつかることもできます。例えば、ゴルフボールほどの小さな岩です。

sentences.en: Hitting that at 20% the speed of light > [ music ] > releases more than double the energy of the nuclear bomb that was dropped over Hiroshima.
sentences.jp: 20%の光速でその物質にぶつかった場合、広島で使用された原爆のエネルギーの2倍以上を放出します。

vocab.note: In this context, 'hitting' refers to the impact of the dust at high speed.
In the context of energy production or emission, 'releases' refers to the act of emitting energy.

sentences.en: We'll not even talk about anything larger.
sentences.jp: さらに大きな物質については話しません。

sentences.en: Atoms, dust, and pebbles are dangerous enough.
sentences.jp: 原子、ほこり、小石はすでに危険です。

vocab.note: Small rocks or stones, commonly used in contexts of physical objects in space or nature.

sentences.en: We might have reached our natural speed limit here.
sentences.jp: ここでは自然の速度制限に達した可能性があります。

sentences.en: Beside the fact that we don't have a good idea how we could possibly fly any faster, all of the damaging effects of hitting stuff floating around in the void get much worse, fast.
sentences.jp: 私たちがさらに速く飛行できる方法がわからない上、宇宙の空でぶつかる物質のダメージが急速に悪化します。

vocab.note: Here used as a preposition meaning 'in addition to' or 'apart from'.
